summary:
ITV Anglia is ITV’s regional service for the East of England, based at Anglia House in Norwich, with news bureaux in Cambridge and Northampton. It broadcasts to parts of nine counties, and its main programme, ITV News Anglia, has East and West editions.

Anglia Television launched on 27 October 1959 as an independent ITV company. It became known for drama and the long-running wildlife series *Survival*. The Belmont transmitter was transferred to Yorkshire Television in 1974, but Anglia retained its franchise in 1980 and added relay stations after viewer protests. It began 24-hour broadcasting in 1987.

The company introduced separate East and West news services in 1990; after a period of pan-regional coverage from 2009, the two editions returned. Anglia changed owners several times from 1994 and became part of ITV plc in 2004, ending as a separate brand. Its Norwich production operations were reduced, and the Magdalen Street studios were sold in 2006. Its distinctive knight-on-horseback ident was replaced in 1988.
